structured_output.what_is_happening: This is one of at least 10 "Effective Accelerationism / e/acc" tokens launched within about an hour. That points to a trigger event, probably a post by Beff Jezos: GeckoTerminal lists a beffjezos status link. This token is an 11-minute-old PumpSwap pool, not a pump.fun curve launch; its deploy platform is unknown. Liquidity was seeded directly at about $30k against about $20k market cap, and 100% of the LP is unlocked with few LP providers. Volume is about $520k in the first hour, 17x the market cap. There are 570 unique buyers and 88 sellers. Price is up about 45% from launch but flat over the last 5 minutes, just under its all-time high.

narrative.description: e/acc (effective accelerationism) meme, likely triggered by a fresh Beff Jezos post. It is a known, recognisable crypto-Twitter culture theme.
narrative.why_spreading: A post from a well-known figure set off a burst of copycat launches. Traders are spreading their money across clones looking for the canonical one.

token_connection.why_this_token: The only link is the ticker and name, plus a GeckoTerminal link to a beffjezos post. There is no website, no socials and no DexScreener profile. It is also one of the later clones in the wave.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 9 same-name clones launched in the same hour. Several are already at $300k–$740k market cap with $1M–$11M hourly volume (7dVW..., 13vV..., 3m7B..., CbcyNo...). One (J246...) shows an $850M market cap with almost no volume, which is probably a fake or misleading listing. There is also an older 2024 pump.fun e/acc token.

authenticity.evidence: 570 unique buyers against 88 sellers and a flat top-10 (about 10% excluding the AMM) suggest broad participation. However, 39 bundler wallets, 17x hourly turnover on a $20k coin, and a dev-seeded unlocked LP on a non-pump.fun pool all point to a manufactured clone set up to catch overflow from the wave.
authenticity.uncertainty: I can't see whether the buyers are real or bot sprays, and I can't tell who controls the LP tokens.

structural_risks: 100% of the LP is unlocked and was seeded by the creator, so it can be pulled at any time
Liquidity is higher than market cap, a typical pattern for pools seeded to be pulled
A late clone competing with larger same-name tokens

structured_output.counterargument: The narrative is hot, and this is the cheapest e/acc on the board at $20k while its siblings sit at $300k–$700k. Buyer breadth is strong (570 against 88) and there is no concentrated holder. If rotation traders go looking for a "cheap e/acc", a 2x from $20k is trivial. The creator holds no tokens, mint and freeze are renounced, and the dev has no prior launches flagged.
unknowns: Who holds the LP tokens, and whether the creator will pull them
Whether the Beff Jezos post endorses any particular contract
Real versus bot share of the 570 buyers
Whether the attention wave is already peaking across clones

source_coverage.notes: No internet in this condition; based only on the evidence packet.

structured_output.thesis: This is a late, non-canonical clone in a crowded e/acc wave. Its LP is unlocked and dev-seeded, liquidity exceeds market cap, and 39 bundler wallets are present. Buyer breadth and the low price give some chance of an overflow pump, but rug risk from an LP pull is high and money in the wave will concentrate in the leading clones.
